findings.title: Capacity-tariff peaks are the top-k metering windows, not the top-k days the tariff bills
findings.claim: tariff.PeakTracker keeps and averages the k highest metering windows regardless of day, so on the only two catalog rows (whose rule is 'the three highest peaks on three different days') a cold morning with three high hours publishes billed_peak_kw 9.80 kW against a true 7.83 kW (+96.37 SEK/month at 49 SEK/kW) and sets threshold_kw 9.60 kW against a true 6.50 kW, so a 9.0 kW hour on another day is priced free by the solver and the live guard while the bill charges 40.83 SEK for it.
findings.mechanism: PeakTracker._close_window appends every closed window to one sorted list; billed_peak_kw averages peaks[:k] and threshold_kw returns peaks[k-1]. Nothing groups by day, so several windows of one day fill the top-k. The plan side (peak_cost) likewise sums the k largest window excesses of the horizon, charging three same-morning windows 3x what one day's single billed peak costs.

findings.title: Entity price sources read unit-blind: öre/kWh or SEK/MWh prices enter the plan 100x/1000x
findings.claim: price_model.prices_from_entity_state and Coordinator._pv_export_price never read the sensor's unit, so a Nord Pool sensor publishing öre/kWh (its price_in_cents option) or SEK/MWh reaches the planning prices at 83.0x / 828.6x the true SEK/kWh (export price 100x / 1000x) while the grid fee, capacity tariff and cycling cost stay in SEK, shrinking the fee's share of the price spread from 0.132 to 0.0015 / 0.00015.
findings.mechanism: prices_from_entity_attributes copies raw_today[].value verbatim (only VAT multiplier and surcharge applied); _pv_export_price floats state.state; neither consults unit_of_measurement or price_in_cents. Coordinator._price_series then adds grid_fee.fee_vector (SEK/kWh) to the unscaled series, and the published predicted_cost/savings carry the resolved HA currency label.
